items.followUp: What is a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack?

rubric.why: Identifies how the attack floods or overloads the target.
rubric.description: Explains that the attacker sends excessive traffic or requests to a computer, server, or network.
rubric.how: Award for describing a flood of traffic or requests that overloads the target.

rubric.why: States the effect on intended users.
rubric.description: Explains that legitimate users cannot access the service or that it becomes unavailable.
rubric.how: Award for stating the resulting service disruption or denial of access.

rubric.why: Recognises that the attack may use multiple devices, as in a DDoS attack.
rubric.description: Mentions that the attack can be launched from many computers or compromised devices.
rubric.how: Award for identifying multiple attacking devices or computers.

rubric.description: States that the aim is to disrupt or deny access to the target's service.
rubric.how: Award for the purpose of denying or disrupting service.

modelAnswer: A Denial of Service (DoS) attack attempts to make a computer, server, or network service unavailable.
The attacker floods the target with excessive traffic or requests, overloading its resources.
As a result, legitimate users may be unable to access the service.
A DoS attack disrupts service; when many compromised computers are used, it is called a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack.

items.followUp: Describe evaluating alternative solutions before choosing one.

rubric.why: Identifies that possible solutions are assessed or compared.
rubric.description: States that alternative solutions are evaluated or compared.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning assessment or comparison of alternatives.

rubric.why: Explains that the choice should meet the problem's needs.
rubric.description: States that the most suitable solution is chosen according to requirements or criteria.
rubric.how: Award for connecting the choice to suitability, requirements, or criteria.

modelAnswer: Evaluate and compare the possible solutions against the problem's requirements or relevant criteria.
Select the solution that is most suitable and effective for solving the problem.

items.followUp: What does a rectangle symbol represent in a flowchart?

rubric.why: Identifies the symbol as a connector.
rubric.description: States that the circle (O) is a connector symbol in a flowchart.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as a connector or continuation symbol.

rubric.description: Explains that it connects or indicates continuation between separated parts of a flowchart.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that it links flowchart sections or shows where the flow continues.

modelAnswer: The O-shaped symbol is a connector in a flowchart.
It links separated parts of the flowchart or shows where the flow continues.

rubric.why: States that verification involves checking a solution.
rubric.description: Defines verification as checking or examining a solution.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as a checking process.

rubric.why: States what the solution is checked against.
rubric.description: Explains that the check determines whether the solution is correct and meets the problem's requirements.
rubric.how: Award for referring to correctness, requirements, or solving the problem.

modelAnswer: Verification is the process of checking a solution to determine whether it is correct.
It checks that the solution meets the problem's requirements.

items.followUp: Name the HTML tags used to make a definition list and its entries.

rubric.why: Identifies the tag that defines the list.
rubric.description: Names the <dl> tag as the definition-list container.

rubric.why: Identifies the tags for terms and their descriptions.
rubric.description: Names <dt> for a term and <dd> for its definition or description.
rubric.how: Award for both entry tags, with their roles understood.

modelAnswer: A definition list presents terms together with their definitions or descriptions.
The <dl> tag defines the list; <dt> marks a term and <dd> gives its definition or description.

items.followUp: Which HTML tag creates a row in a table?

rubric.why: Identifies the HTML tag used for a table data cell.
rubric.description: Writes the <td> tag used to create a data cell in a table.

rubric.why: Shows the tag's role in building a table column.
rubric.description: Explains that table cells in rows form the table's columns.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the cell contributes to a column.

modelAnswer: Use the <td> tag to create a table data cell.
Cells placed in table rows form the columns of the table.

items.followUp: Give one example each of volatile and non-volatile memory.

rubric.why: States the defining property of volatile memory.
rubric.description: Explains that volatile memory loses its contents when power is switched off.
rubric.how: Award for the loss of data when power is removed.

rubric.why: States the defining property of non-volatile memory.
rubric.description: Explains that non-volatile memory retains its contents without power.
rubric.how: Award for the retention of data when power is removed.

modelAnswer: Volatile memory loses its stored data when the power is switched off; RAM is an example.
Non-volatile memory retains its data without power; ROM is an example.

items.followUp: Convert (101101)₂ into the decimal number system.

rubric.why: Shows the binary digits expanded using powers of two.
rubric.description: Writes the place-value expansion of the binary number.
rubric.how: Award for a correct expansion or its evaluated place values.
